draft.title: Megacities
card: A megacity is a city with more than 10 million people. The word describes size only, not how rich or well run a city is.
Most megacities are now in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Examples include Tokyo, Delhi, Lagos and São Paulo.
In some megacities, many people live in informal settlements. These are areas where homes are built without legal title to the land or official approval.
Informal settlements often have poor access to services such as clean water, sewerage and electricity. This happens when a city grows faster than it can supply housing and services.
draft.remember: A megacity is defined by size, over 10 million people. Some have large informal settlements.

a.q: What makes a city a megacity?
opts: It has more than 10 million people
It has a large area of informal settlements
It is the capital city of a country
It has the highest income per person in its region
a.why: A megacity is defined by population size alone, more than 10 million people. Informal settlements are found in some megacities, but they do not decide whether a city is one.
a.clue: Think about the number of people, not the type of housing.

b.q: Kavita says that any megacity must have large informal settlements. Why is she wrong?
opts: Megacity means size only, and only some have them
Informal settlements are found only in small towns
Megacities are all located in wealthy countries
Informal settlements are legal and planned by councils
b.why: A megacity is defined by having over 10 million people, so it can exist without large informal settlements. Some do have them, but that is not part of the definition.
b.clue: Check what the definition of a megacity includes.

a.best: It has more than 10 million people

b.best: Megacity means size only, and only some have them

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about the number of people, not the type of housing' points straight to the population option and rules out the informal-settlements distractor, so a student can answer without knowing the definition.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are sound. The only issue is that question a's clue names population outright, which gives the answer away.
